close_reason: P0-P2 fixes complete; P3/P4 sub-issues remain as backlog
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — two public API traps (auth context silently dropped, structured header forms silently return null), one OOM vector, one collision-prone ID generator, and a pervasive update_object return value pattern that will produce non-conformant responses the moment any backend starts returning server-modified fields
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug.   Least confident flags: JMAP-yqo.4 (Email/import new_state may be intentional for RFC compliance — re-check §5.7 wording); JMAP-yqo.5 (concurrent delete scenario is real but MemoryBackend is single-process so only matters for production backends).   Uncertainty driven by: could not read the full RFC 8621 §5.7 and §4.9 spec text to independently verify all property lists; did not trace all 117 test cases to verify complete coverage of edge cases in submission.rs; did not inspect vacation.rs and identity.rs in depth (assumed same patterns as email.rs).   Would raise confidence if: ran the test suite with a backend that returns Some(O) from update_object to confirm the echo-discard bug triggers visibly; verified RFC 8621 §5.8 wording on header: support in Email/parse.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — The codebase is functionally well-structured with #[forbid(unsafe_code)], #[non_exhaustive] on public enums, and consistent error propagation patterns. No unsafe code exists. The main idiom complaints are: .expect() calls in library handlers (vacation.rs/snippet.rs) that should use map_err; a Display impl for SetErrorType that maintains a parallel exhaustive match instead of delegating to serde; HeaderForm missing Display causing Debug identifiers in user-facing error strings; and pervasive clone-heavy patterns in property filtering that a by-value refactor would eliminate. None of these are unsound but a serious Rust practitioner would raise them in review.
Rust idiom confidence: 80% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-yqo.28 (ClosureHandler call_id String — depends on whether jmap-server HandlerFuture trait could accept &str; could not inspect that crate's JmapHandler trait signature in detail), JMAP-yqo.34 (validate_and_normalize_keywords — the by-value signature may be intentional to avoid a separate clone at the call site). Uncertainty driven by: email.rs is 1600+ lines; read in 400-line chunks so may have missed patterns in the Email/import and Email/copy sections not covered here; did not read the remaining ~500 lines of common/mod.rs covering FaultyBackend and filter helper functions.
